I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation that I know best. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to earn a steady harvest from one year to the next. I am 65, so I will not choose crops that need too much hand labor or complicated field management. I will grow winter wheat first, because it fits our land and water conditions and gives me a reliable grain crop. After harvesting wheat, I will sow summer maize on the same land, because it follows well after wheat, uses the summer heat and rain, and I am familiar with how to manage it.

I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps me get even emergence and stable yield, but I will still manage the field in the simple way I trust: basal fertilizer, a few topdressings, timely irrigation, and only the pesticide sprays I think are necessary to protect the crop. I will not overcomplicate tillage. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is easier to arrange and lighter work than deep ploughing every season. My goal is not the highest possible yield on paper; my goal is a stable harvest, manageable labor, and lower risk.
